title: How Non-US Residents Can Open a Mercury or Relay Business Bank Account Without a SSN or ITIN
content:
# How Non-US Residents Can Open a Mercury or Relay Business Bank Account Without a SSN or ITIN

If you're a non-U.S. resident running an American LLC, you already know the frustration: most banking guides assume you have a Social Security Number. You don't. And that's fine — because Mercury and Relay have quietly become the go-to banking solutions for international founders who need a legitimate U.S. business bank account without jumping through impossible hoops.

This guide walks you through exactly what you need, what to expect, and how to avoid the mistakes that get applications rejected.

---

## Why U.S. Business Banking Matters for Non-Residents

A U.S. bank account isn't a nice-to-have. It's the backbone of your American business operation.

Without one, you can't receive ACH payments, set up Stripe or PayPal properly, pay U.S. vendors, or build the financial credibility that enterprise clients expect. Your LLC is legally real — but without a bank account, it's operationally invisible.

The good news? You don't need an SSN or ITIN to open a business bank account. You need the **right bank** and the **right documents**.

> **Note:** An ITIN (Individual Taxpayer Identification Number) is different from an EIN (Employer Identification Number). For business banking as a non-resident, your **EIN is the critical number** — not an SSN or ITIN.

---

## Mercury vs. Relay: Which Bank Is Right for You?

Both Mercury and Relay are financial technology companies (not traditional banks) that offer FDIC-insured accounts. Here's how they compare at a glance:

| Feature | Mercury | Relay |
|---|---|---|
| **Account Type** | Business Checking & Savings | Business Checking |
| **Monthly Fee** | $0 (Standard) | $0 (Standard) / $30 (Pro) |
| **Non-Resident Friendly** | ✅ Yes | ✅ Yes |
| **EIN Required** | ✅ Yes | ✅ Yes |
| **SSN/ITIN Required** | ❌ No | ❌ No |
| **Debit Cards** | ✅ Virtual + Physical | ✅ Virtual + Physical |
| **ACH & Wire Transfers** | ✅ Yes | ✅ Yes |
| **Sub-Accounts** | ✅ Up to 3 (Standard) | ✅ Up to 20 |
| **Integrations** | Stripe, QuickBooks, Gusto | QuickBooks, Xero, Plaid |
| **Best For** | Startups, SaaS, Funded companies | Freelancers, agencies, cash-flow management |

> **Note:** Both Mercury and Relay partner with FDIC-insured banks (Mercury with Choice Financial Group & Evolve Bank; Relay with Thread Bank). Your deposits are insured up to $250,000 USD.

**Choose Mercury if** you want a sleek interface, startup-friendly features, and seamless integration with payment processors like Stripe.

**Choose Relay if** you want granular cash-flow control, multiple sub-accounts for expense budgeting, and strong accounting software integrations.

Many international founders use **both** — Mercury as their primary receiving account and Relay for operational expense management.

---

## What You Need Before You Apply

Get these documents ready before you even open the application. Missing even one will stall or kill your application.

### Required for Both Mercury and Relay

- ✅ **A registered U.S. LLC** (fully formed, with a registered agent)
- ✅ **EIN (Employer Identification Number)** — issued by the IRS, confirmed via CP-575 notice or 147C letter
- ✅ **LLC Articles of Organization** — the official formation document from your state
- ✅ **Valid passport** — for each beneficial owner (anyone owning 25%+ of the company)
- ✅ **U.S. business address** — your registered agent address works; do NOT use a P.O. Box
- ✅ **Personal address** — your actual residential address (outside the U.S. is fine)
- ✅ **Company Operating Agreement** — especially critical for single-member LLCs

### Optional but Strongly Recommended

- 📄 **EIN Confirmation Letter (CP-575 or 147C)** — a PDF or clear photo of this letter significantly speeds up verification
- 📄 **Website or LinkedIn Profile** — Mercury in particular may request proof of your business activity

> **Note:** If your EIN was obtained verbally over the phone (common for non-residents), you may only have a handwritten EIN number, not a formal letter. Request your **147C letter** by calling the IRS at +1-800-829-4933. This is the official replacement letter for the CP-575 and banks accept it universally.

---

## Step-by-Step: How to Apply to Mercury

### Step 1 — Go to Mercury.com and Create an Account

Navigate to mercury.com and click **"Open an Account."** You'll create a personal login first using your email address. No SSN is required at this stage.

### Step 2 — Select Your Business Type

Choose **LLC** as your business structure. Mercury will ask about your business category — select the option that most accurately reflects your work (software, consulting, e-commerce, etc.).

### Step 3 — Enter Your Business Information

Fill in:
- Legal business name (exactly as it appears on your Articles of Organization)
- Business EIN
- State of formation
- Registered business address

### Step 4 — Add Beneficial Owners

You'll be asked to list all beneficial owners (anyone with 25%+ ownership). For each owner, you'll provide:
- Full legal name
- Date of birth
- Nationality
- Passport number and copy
- Country of residence

> **Note:** You will **not** be asked for an SSN here if you are a non-U.S. resident. Mercury's system recognizes international founders. If the form insists on an SSN field, select "I don't have an SSN" or enter your passport details instead.

### Step 5 — Upload Your Documents

Upload clear, legible copies of:
- Your LLC Articles of Organization
- Your EIN confirmation letter (CP-575 or 147C)
- Your passport (government-issued, valid)
- Operating Agreement (if requested)

### Step 6 — Submit and Wait for Review

Mercury's review typically takes **2–7 business days** for non-resident applications. You may receive an email asking for additional documentation — respond promptly to avoid delays.

Once approved, your account is live. You'll receive a virtual debit card immediately and a physical card shipped to a U.S. address (or internationally in some cases).

---

## Step-by-Step: How to Apply to Relay

### Step 1 — Go to RelayFi.com and Sign Up

Navigate to relayfi.com and click **"Get Started."** Like Mercury, you'll create an account with your email — no SSN required upfront.

### Step 2 — Enter Your Business Details

Provide:
- Legal LLC name
- EIN
- State of formation
- Business address (your registered agent address works)

### Step 3 — Verify Beneficial Owners

Similar to Mercury, Relay requires information on all beneficial owners (25%+ ownership):
- Full name, date of birth, and nationality
- Government-issued ID (passport)
- Residential address (non-U.S. addresses are accepted)

### Step 4 — Upload Supporting Documents

Relay typically requests:
- Articles of Organization
- EIN letter
- Passport copy

Relay's interface has a clean document upload portal. Label your files clearly (e.g., `LLC_Articles_StateName.pdf`) to help their review team process faster.

### Step 5 — Wait for Approval

Relay's review for non-residents takes **3–7 business days** on average. Approval rates are strong when documentation is complete and consistent.

Once approved, you can immediately open up to 20 checking accounts within your Relay dashboard — a standout feature for budget-conscious operators.

---

## Common Reasons Applications Get Rejected (And How to Avoid Them)

Most rejections are preventable. Here's what goes wrong:

| Mistake | Why It's a Problem | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| **Business name mismatch** | Your name on the application doesn't exactly match your Articles of Organization | Use the exact legal name, including "LLC" |
| **PO Box as business address** | Banks flag P.O. boxes as high-risk | Use your registered agent's street address |
| **No EIN letter** | Verbal EIN without documentation creates verification failures | Request 147C from IRS before applying |
| **Blurry or cropped passport** | Document review requires a full, clear image | Scan or photograph your full passport photo page |
| **Inconsistent ownership info** | Name or DOB doesn't match your ID | Triple-check all personal details before submitting |
| **High-risk business category** | Some industries trigger enhanced review | Be accurate but choose the closest, most descriptive category |

> **Note:** If you are rejected, both Mercury and Relay allow you to reapply. Fix the specific issue mentioned in their rejection email, wait 30 days, and resubmit with clean documentation.

---

## What Happens After Approval: Setting Up Your Account for Business

Getting approved is step one. Here's how to make your account operational from day one.

### Connect Your Payment Processor

Link your Mercury or Relay account to Stripe, PayPal, or Wise. This is where most non-resident founders start receiving revenue.

### Set Up ACH Details

Share your U.S. **routing number** and **account number** with clients who pay by bank transfer. This establishes you as a legitimate U.S. business entity in their system.

### Order Your Physical Debit Card

Mercury ships physical cards internationally (timeline varies). Relay's physical card ships to a U.S. address, so you may need a U.S. forwarding address or a trusted contact.

### Enable Two-Factor Authentication

Protect your account immediately. Both platforms support authenticator apps — use one. Never rely solely on SMS-based 2FA.

### Consider a Wise Business Account as a Companion

A [Wise Business](https://wise.com/business) multi-currency account pairs exceptionally well with Mercury or Relay. Use Wise to receive and convert international payments before routing USD to your U.S. bank account.

---

## Frequently Asked Questions

### Can I open a Mercury or Relay account if my LLC is in Wyoming or New Mexico?

Yes. Both banks accept LLCs formed in all 50 states. Wyoming and New Mexico are popular choices for non-residents, and both are well-recognized by Mercury and Relay.

### Do I need a U.S. phone number?

A U.S. phone number is helpful but not strictly required. Both platforms accept international phone numbers for account verification.

### Can a multi-member LLC apply?

Yes. Each beneficial owner (25%+ stake) will need to provide their passport and personal information. All members must complete their portion of the KYC (Know Your Customer) verification.

### Will my account be in USD?

Yes. Both Mercury and Relay accounts are USD-denominated. For multi-currency needs, pair with a Wise Business account.

### What if my application is stuck in review for more than 10 days?

Email Mercury or Relay support directly and reference your application ID. Proactively offering to submit additional documentation usually speeds up the process. Mercury has a notably responsive support team.

---

## The Complete Pre-Application Checklist

Use this before you hit "Submit" on either application:

- [ ] LLC is fully registered and in good standing
- [ ] EIN confirmed with CP-575 or 147C letter (PDF ready)
- [ ] Articles of Organization ready as a clear PDF
- [ ] Operating Agreement prepared
- [ ] Passport valid (at least 6 months remaining)
- [ ] Passport photo page scanned at high resolution
- [ ] Business address confirmed (registered agent street address, not P.O. Box)
- [ ] Personal residential address confirmed (non-U.S. is fine)
- [ ] Business description prepared (2–3 sentences about what your company does)
- [ ] All beneficial owner information consistent across all documents

---
